To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
collagen sponges are not a suitable carrier system for antibiotics with long-term effects.
collagen implants saturated with antibiotics are suitable as a short-term antibiotic release system.

the collagen implant saturated in antibiotic solution and the collagen sponge containing gentamycin are not suitable for the treatment of infections in bone defects, because of the low drug delivery rate of both systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials that are suitable for the treatment of infected areas.
the development of a collagen implant for local antibiotic treatment in infected wounds.
the development of collagen materials for the controlled release of antibiotics in the treatment of wound infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the collagen implants are unsuitable for the delivery of antibiotics.
the collagen implant saturated with antibiotic solutions is suitable as a local carrier of antibiotic in infected areas for 24-48h.
a collagen sponge containing gentamycin sulphate is not suitable as a carrier for antibiotics in the treatment of infected wounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
collagen materials are not a suitable substitute for antibiotic therapy in the treatment of infected wounds.
the collagen implants saturated in the antibiotic solutions are suitable only for a very short period of antibiotic release, and the collagen sponge with gentamicin is not suitable at all.
the collagen sponge is a suitable material for the delivery of antibiotics in the form of a depot, but not for a short-term release.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collagen implant saturated with antibiotic solution is not suitable for use in cases of infected tissue.
the collagen sponge containing gentamycin is the most promising material for the delivery of gentamycin.
the collagen sponge is the only suitable material for the long-term delivery of antibiotics.
